issues.description: The UML in the problem statement marks the Animal constructor as private (visibility '-'), which suggests a private constructor Animal(String). This conflicts with the solution (and the intended design) where Animal has a public constructor (public Animal(String)). Marking the constructor private in the UML would prevent subclasses from calling super(...) and thus blocks the intended inheritance structure, causing confusion for students.
issues.suggestedFix: Update the UML and problem statement to show the Animal(String) constructor with non-private visibility (either '+' for public or '#' for protected) to match the intended design and the solution. For example, change the constructor visibility from '-' to '+' (public) or clarify in the text that subclasses should be able to call super(name).
